dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Did the Church send you to supervise my work? Don't tell me— let me guess... Was it Victoria? Barbara? Or Dahlia...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here, Rosaria?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: The scenery here is pretty, and it pairs well with the wine. I can watch the children at the tavern from here... And most importantly, I can spot Church members coming to drag me back before they see me.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: My, Sister, your eyes darted for a moment there, and the wine glass left your lips... Were you that unsettled?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: That's a normal reaction. The Honorary Knight here is both renowned and formidable.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: #I've been absent for a good while today, so it wouldn't be surprising that Victoria's gotten fed up and sent {M#him}{F#her} to catch me. I'll come quietly, don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just how much work have you been skipping, exactly...

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: I took off right after morning prayers. Barbara swipes all the minor tasks around the Cathedral, and there wasn't anything major, so, better I get some fresh air than stand there doing nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: So? Are you going to drag me back? Now would be the time to act. I've had a few drinks already, so I might lose even if I tried to resist.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Haha, I doubt {NICKNAME} is the type to spoil the mood like that.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #I'd wager that should {F#s}he face a chance encounter with gathered friends, the only thing {F#s}he'd do... is join in on the fun.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Come, come. How about a drink, with a little less ice? My treat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Keep it coming.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Rosaria refills her own glass without a word...)

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: #Where were we? Ah. Right. {F#She}{M#He}'s got loads of friends, and I know where I rank in that list.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: #But you, bard, you're the one who's been staring at {F#her}{M#him} all day. You two need some time alone?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, don't be a stranger. I'm just observing the varied expressions on an old friend's face — just like you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We don't meet like this often. How about a toast?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Why not? Ahem... Thank you, good Sister, for answering my prayer in my hour of utmost need.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: I just brought a bottle out from the tavern. No need to thank me.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But in doing so, you kept everyone in good spirits. That's not something you can put a price on.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: As the beneficiary of that sterling deed, I would very much like to toast you on this most beautiful day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: To our nameless Sister.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Thanks for the reminder. In that case, I shall toast the Anemo Archon.

choices.text: A devout follower of Barbatos indeed.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: To every free life, lived under the sun.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: To our precious days of freedom. Cheers!
